text: For three hundred years, I swept the gate of the Great King's cave.
Leaves in autumn. Snow in winter. Bones, mostly, the rest of the year.
The Great King had a hundred demons. A hundred names.
Iron Tusk. Seven Eyes. Mister Fang.
asr: Iron Tusk. Seven Eyes. Mr. Fang.

text: Nobody ever asked mine.
You! Broom thing! Sweep faster!
I do not think he knew I had one.
Every morning, the demons marched down the mountain to frighten the villages.
Every evening, they marched back, and the gate was dirty again.
So I swept. That is what I was for.
Some nights, I swept the moon off the pond.
It always came back. I liked that about it.
Then came the summer of the great rain.
The mountain is falling! Every demon for himself!
The Great King was the first to run. He is very brave, normally.
A hundred demons, gone in a hundred directions.
I stayed. Nobody had told me to stop sweeping.
That was when I heard it. Crying, under the old pine.
Is someone there? I can't find the path home.
A human child. Lost, and soaked, and smaller than my broom.
Demons are meant to frighten children.
I had never frightened anyone. I didn't know where to start.
Are you… a monster?
I… sweep.
The water was rising. The path down the mountain was gone, under mud and broken trees.
So I did the only thing I know.
By morning, the rain had stopped.
At the bottom of the mountain, the child's village was waiting with lanterns.
Thank you. What's your name?
Three hundred years. Nobody had ever asked.
I don't… have one.
Then I'll give you one. You swept the whole night away.
I'll call you Sweep.
Sweep.
It is not a grand name. Not like Iron Tusk, or Mister Fang.
asr: It is not a grand name. Not like Iron Tusk, or Mr. Fang.

text: But it was given to me. And it was mine.
The Great King came back, of course. He always does.
You! Broom thing!
Sweep, sir. My name is Sweep.
And every morning now, someone at the bottom of the mountain waves.
